summary: Procurement call to review MSA and DPA terms, SLA expectations and pricing approval path. Redwood AE/SE walked through key clauses and proposed SLA appendix. Customer legal/CTO raised data residency and KMS requirements; security asked for SOC2 and pen test schedule. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlines + security package; schedule technical demo for benchmarking.
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-04-05 | Time: 16:00 PT | Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Diana (Celesta Procurement), Amir (CTO), Sanjay (Legal), Ellen (Vendor Ops), Ravi (Security)

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Hi Diana, Amir, Sanjay, Ellen, Ravi — appreciate you making time.
00:08 Diana: Thanks Maya, yeah we've got about an hour blocked, main thing is we need to make progress on the MSA and DPA and align on SLAs and pricing approvals.
00:16 Maya: Totally. Quick agenda: go through the MSA redlines we pre-shared, call out any DPA concerns, then Jonas will walk high-level SLOs and suggested appendix for latency/uptime, final block for pricing and next steps.
00:28 Amir: Sounds good. Also we'll want to verify the private deployment options — VPC and key management — before exec sign-off.
00:35 Jonas: Yep, we'll cover KMS and VPC flow. Quick note, apologies if transcript is a bit rough, my connection is a bit laggy.

02:12 Maya: On the MSA we flagged three main asks: 1) data ownership and IP carveouts, 2) indemnity limits, 3) termination for convenience timeline. We proposed edits in the Google doc — link: [MSA draft - redline link].
02:27 Sanjay: On indemnity, Celesta's legal generally pushes for mutual indemnity for IP, and we need clarity on data breach timelines. Also Data Processing Appendix — we need stricter deletion windows for PHI derivative data.
02:40 Maya: Understood. Our standard DPA offers 30 day deletion on request and 90 day backups retention, but we can discuss tighter windows for PHI under the private deployment option.
03:05 Ravi: On security, two things: KMS/HSM integration for keys, and audit logs retention. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS and forward audit logs to our Splunk?
03:18 Jonas: Yes — we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) on the Private line and Dedicated. For hosted we have managed KMS but can offer envelope encryption; for Dedicated/Private you can supply keys. We have an audit-forwarding agent, link: [security pack]. Small footnote, we need to validate Splunk collector version.

05:02 Diana: Pricing — the finance committee needs a pricing worksheet with committed monthly usage tiers and breakpoints, plus an expected runway to hit the dedicated-capacity threshold.
05:14 Maya: We'll send the pricing worksheet. Quick question: what is a realistic initial commit you're expecting?
05:20 Diana: We're targeting 1M tokens per month to start but may ramp to 5-10M in six months if latency looks good.
05:30 Jonas: For 1M tokens, hosted API is fine; for 5M+ we usually recommend dedicated or reserved GPU pools to control latency and cost; we'll provide model-specific TCO.

07:45 Amir: On SLAs, our apps have 99.95% availability target and 95th/99th percentile latency goals under 300ms for small prompts and sub-second for longer seqs. Can Redwood commit to those in an appendix?
07:59 Jonas: Our Dedicated tiers can support 99.95% uptime SLA and we can propose latency SLOs in the appendix. We do need to clarify measurement windows and which endpoints (streaming vs non-stream). We'll propose 99th pct latency targets and a credit schedule.
08:24 Sanjay: Also need to see the incident response timeline and escalation matrix.
08:30 Lina: We'll attach our standard incident and escalation playbook and can map to Celesta's on the appendix.

10:12 Ellen: For procurement timing, our internal approvals require legal sign-off and a budget owner approval. Once legal clears the MSA/DPA, pricing approval goes to the finance committee which meets Tuesdays. If Redwood can get redlines in by next Wed (04/08), we could potentially review 04/14.
10:30 Maya: That timeline works; we'll prioritize the redline and security pack next week.

12:55 Jonas: Technical note on private deployment and data residency: we can deploy the control plane in a customer VPC and ensure model payloads don't cross regions. For PHI workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated with encryption at rest and customer-managed KMS. There is a slight latency tax for on-prem but better for residency and compliance.
13:18 Ravi: Ok, we will need a network diagram and ports list to feed to our infra team.
13:25 Jonas: We'll include an architecture diagram and a port/IP list in the security pack.

15:40 Sanjay: A couple DPA specifics: sub processors list and 3rd party data sharing — we need a clause to notify us 30 days before adding a new subprocessor.
15:55 Maya: That's reasonable; our standard is notification and an opt-out path for high-risk processors. We'll add the 30 day notice language.

18:22 Diana: On audits, Celesta will likely request SOC2 and a pen test report — do you have a recent pen test complement and SOC2 Type II window?
18:33 Lina: We have SOC2 Type II (2025) and have an internal pen test schedule; we can share redacted reports and the SOC2 pack.

20:05 Amir: One more technical ask — KV cache handling and prefix caching: we need determinism around how tokens are cached when sessions are resumed, for compliance tracking.
20:20 Jonas: We can provide documentation on KV cache TTLs and session sealing. For strict compliance we recommend Dedicated with KV cache pinned per customer namespace.

23:00 Maya: Pricing note: we'll provide a committed and metered option with breakpoints and a pilot discount. Also we'll include an appendix for overage billing.
23:12 Diana: Good. Also please call out any termination for convenience fees; finance needs to know exit costs.
23:22 Maya: We'll be explicit in the pricing worksheet and MSA — typical termination language and any early termination fees for Reserved capacity.

28:45 Sanjay: A few minor redlines on liability caps and warranty language — I'll mark those in the doc and return.
28:55 Maya: Perfect. Appreciate that.

33:10 Jonas: For the live benchmark/demo, we'll simulate 99th pct loads and provide expected GPU sizing — want us to test in Celesta's stage VPC or Redwood demo infra?
33:25 Amir: Prefer in our stage VPC to validate network egress and latency, but if it's easier initially on Redwood infra that's ok for a quick baseline.
33:38 Jonas: We'll propose two runs: baseline on Redwood infra, and a run in Celesta stage VPC. Schedule week of 04/13.

40:00 Maya: Ok to recap — action items: Redwood sends MSA/DPA redline and pricing worksheet + security pack by 04/08, Jonas to prepare benchmark plan by 04/09, Celesta to return legal redlines by 04/10 and share vendor questionnaire by 04/07.
40:18 Diana: Yes that's right. We'll route the redlines internally and get procurement calendar slots.
40:30 Sanjay: Thank you, I'll try to get initial redlines by Friday but worst case 04/10.

51:00 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with the documents and a calendar invite for the benchmarking demo.
51:08 Diana: Thanks Maya, talk soon.
51:12 (call ends)
